[T]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & -3\end{aligned}],\,{P}_{C\to B}=[\begin{aligned}5 & 6 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]

Consider the matrix $[T]_{C}$ of a linear transformation $T$ with respect to the basis $C$ and the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{C\to B}$ shown above. Find the matrix of $T$ relative to the basis $B.$

Consider the matrix $[\mathbf{T}]_{\mathcal{B}}$ of a linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ with respect to the basis $\mathcal{B}$ and the change-of-coordinates matrix $P_{\small \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{C}}$ shown above. Find the matrix of $\mathbf{T}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{C}.$
examples.worked_solution:
The connection between the matrices of our linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ relative to the bases $\mathcal{B}$ and $\mathcal{C}$ is given by the following diagram:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14067267/assets/1b81504d6fdcabee0e1f586fef3dd2af5a57a8411ba4d22429e00e09b171a4d1.png)

 

Here, moving along an arrow means pre-multiplying by the corresponding matrix. Algebraically, we can write this as

$$
[\mathbf{T}]_{\mathcal{C}} = P_{\small{\mathcal{B}}\to{\mathcal{C}}} \cdot [\mathbf{T}]_{\mathcal{B}} \cdot P_{\small{\mathcal{B}}\to{\mathcal{C}}}^{-1}\,,
$$

where $P_{\small{\mathcal{B}}\to{\mathcal{C}}}$ is the change-of-coordinates matrix from $\mathcal{B}$ to $\mathcal{C}.$

Our goal is to compute $[\mathbf{T}]_{\mathcal{C}}.$ First, we compute the inverse of $P_{\small{\mathcal{B}}\to{\mathcal{C}}} \mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{B\to C}^{-1} & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{1\cdot 1-0\cdot (-1)}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can compute the matrix of $\mathbf{T}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{C} \mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}[T]_{C} & ={P}_{B\to C}\cdot [T]_{B}\cdot {P}_{B\to C}^{-1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 5 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & -7 \\ 5 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & -10 \\ 5 & 9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Let $[T]_{B}$ and $[T]_{C}$ be the matrices of a linear transformation $T$ relative to the bases $B$ and $C,$ respectively. If ${P}_{C\to B}$ is the change-of-coordinates matrix from basis $C$ to basis $B,$ which of the following statements are true?

- $[T]_{B}={P}_{C\to B}\cdot [T]_{C}\cdot {P}_{C\to B}^{-1}$
- $[T]_{B}=[T]_{C}^{-1}\cdot {P}_{C\to B}\cdot [T]_{C}$
- $[T]_{C}={P}_{C\to B}\cdot [T]_{B}\cdot {P}_{C\to B}^{-1}$
feedback.worked_solution:
The connection between the matrices of our linear transformation $T$ relative to the bases $B$ and $C$ is given by the following diagram:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14067267/assets/9ba3d1f0eebdfc82c40f36bdbe16896ca15516b623c695b72c331861955329bc.png)

Here, moving along an arrow means pre-multiplying by the corresponding matrix. Algebraically, we can write this as

$$
[T]_{C}={P}_{C\to B}^{-1}\cdot [T]_{B}\cdot {P}_{C\to B},
$$

where ${P}_{C\to B}$ is the change-of-coordinates matrix from $C$ to $B.$

Solving this equation for $[T]_{B},$ we obtain the alternative formulation

$$
[T]_{B}={P}_{C\to B}\cdot [T]_{C}\cdot {P}_{C\to B}^{-1}.
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
